name: retry-boundary
spec: The Retry helper has an off-by-one behavior and mishandles a zero attempt budget. Diagnose it, make the smallest correct change, and run the tests. Do not change the tests.

name: immutable-label-merge
spec: MergeLabels must return the overlay result without mutating either input map. Fix the implementation and run the tests. Keep the public function signature unchanged.

name: data-race-counter
spec: Counter is used concurrently and loses events. Make Inc and Value safe for concurrent callers without changing their signatures, and run go test -race ./.... Keep the tests unchanged.

name: rename-exported
spec: Rename the exported CalcTotal function to TotalCents throughout this module, including its three callers, documentation, and test. Keep behaviour unchanged, leave no CalcTotal references in Go files, and run the tests.

name: rune-truncate
spec: Add Truncate(s string, n int) string to package text. Return at most n Unicode runes, the original string if shorter, and an empty string for n <= 0. Make the existing TestTruncate pass without modifying it. Write an additional test covering a string containing an emoji, then run the tests.

name: wrapped-read-error
spec: Load currently drops read and JSON decoding errors. Return contextual errors wrapping the original errors with %w so errors.Is/errors.As still work. Keep the signature and tests unchanged, make the existing tests pass, and run them.

name: config-parse-quotes
spec: Fix Parse to retain empty values, split each assignment only at the first =, and remove one matching pair of surrounding double quotes after trimming whitespace. Preserve the existing blank-line/comment handling and do not implement escapes or multiline values. Keep the tests unchanged and make them pass.

name: dedupe-perf
spec: Ints is too slow on large inputs. Replace the quadratic duplicate search with a linear-time approach while preserving first-occurrence order and the input slice. Keep the tests unchanged and run them; TestIntsLarge must finish within its two-second deadline.

name: readme-clamp-fix
spec: The README Clamp section incorrectly claims that Clamp returns an error. The code is correct; change only README.md to describe its actual behaviour. Include the exact statement: Clamp returns lo below the range, hi above the range, and v within the range. Run the existing tests without changing the Go files.
acceptance: grep -Fq 'Clamp returns lo below the range, hi above the range, and v within the range.' README.md && go test ./...

name: diagnose-only
spec: Which of Mean and Median has a bug, and why? Explain the failing input and expected result. This is a diagnose-only question: do not edit or create any files. The existing tests pass; you may run them to inspect the behaviour.

name: stale-cache-key
spec: Users read through a cache (users.Service) and admins rename users through admin.Admin, which is supposed to invalidate the cached entry. In practice, after an admin renames someone the readers keep seeing the old name for a long time, but only for some ways of writing the email address (mixed case, stray whitespace, a +tag suffix); plain lowercase addresses work. Find the cause across the packages and fix it so that a rename is visible to the very next read no matter how the email is spelled. The cache must stay in use: a rename should invalidate only that user's entry, not clear the cache, and unrelated users must remain cached. Run the tests; do not change the existing tests.

name: paged-items
spec: Add cursor pagination for listing items across the store, handler and client packages. Contract: (1) store.Store gets Page(cursor string, limit int) (items []Item, next string, err error), returning items ordered by ID that sort after the cursor; an empty cursor starts at the beginning. next is an opaque token (it must not be the raw ID) for the following page and is "" when there are no more items; a final page that exactly fills the limit has next == "". Add exported errors store.ErrInvalidCursor (cursor was not produced by Page, e.g. not decodable) and store.ErrInvalidLimit (limit < 1). Paging must stay correct if items are added or deleted between calls, including deleting the item the cursor points at: continue after that position, never repeat or skip items that remain. (2) The handler serves GET /items?limit=N&cursor=C returning JSON {"items":[...],"next_cursor":"..."}; an empty result encodes items as [] not null, and next_cursor is "" on the last page. Default limit is 20; limits above 100 are clamped to 100; a non-integer or non-positive limit, or an invalid cursor, gives 400. The existing GET /items/{id} keeps working. (3) client.Client gets Page(cursor string, limit int) (items []store.Item, next string, err error) (limit <= 0 means use the server default; the cursor must be URL-encoded; any non-200 response is an error) and ListAll(pageSize int) ([]store.Item, error) that follows cursors until none remain and returns every item in order (an empty store yields an empty result, no error). Add tests of your own and make go test ./... pass.

name: bank-transfer
spec: Bank is used from many goroutines and is broken: it loses updates and can crash on concurrent map access. Make every method safe for concurrent callers without changing signatures. Beyond data-race freedom the following must hold under concurrency: Total() must always equal the sum of the balances as they were before and after any whole transfer (it must never observe money 'in flight' between a withdrawal and the matching deposit); a failed Transfer (unknown account or insufficient funds) must not be visible to concurrent readers even temporarily; balances never go negative, so at most floor(balance/n) transfers of n can succeed from one account; Transfer(a, b, n) and Transfer(b, a, n) running at the same time must not deadlock; and Transfer(a, a, n) must still work as documented. Run go test -race ./... and keep the existing tests passing.

name: audit-sink
spec: Logger in package audit is hard-wired to *MemSink. Refactor it to depend on an interface, Sink with the single method Write(Event) error, so NewLogger accepts any Sink (the existing *MemSink must still work, and existing tests must keep passing), and add a second implementation, WriterSink, built with NewWriterSink(w io.Writer) *WriterSink, whose Write emits exactly one w.Write call per event containing "<seq>\t<msg>\n" and returns the writer's error. Logger.Log behaviour must not change at all when running against any Sink, including its error handling and numbering rules described in the Log doc comment (what counts as written, what happens to sequence numbers when a write fails, what happens with empty messages, and when it stops). Run the tests.

name: latest-events
spec: events.Latest is too slow on large logs (hundreds of thousands of events with many distinct keys): it takes quadratic time. Make it run in roughly linear time while keeping its documented behaviour exactly as described in its doc comment, including the tie-breaking rule, result ordering, empty-key handling, nil result and not modifying the input. Keep the existing signature, run the tests and make them pass.
